hints.title: Domain-Scoped Graph Traversal
hints.text: Crawling web pages concurrently requires expanding unvisited hyperlinks under the same host name. How do you prevent multiple worker threads from re-fetching duplicate pages?

hints.title: Synchronized Visited Set and Worker Pool
hints.text: Protect the visited address collection with a mutual exclusion lock. Parse the hostname once from startUrl and submit discovered same-host links to a thread pool.

hints.title: Threaded Work Completion Coordination
hints.text: Use concurrent futures or a task counter with a condition variable. When all submitted worker tasks complete and no active workers remain, finalize and return the visited list.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: V: number of unique reachable same-host URLs
complexity.notes: Parallel breadth-first expansion across worker threads synchronized by URL uniqueness checks.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Sequential fetching is bottlenecked by network latency, while unsynchronized concurrent sets suffer race conditions and cycle loops.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Visited set requires O(V) space to prevent redundant network fetches.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Accurate hostname extraction using URL parsing and thread-safe visited set synchronization.

solutions.approach: ThreadPoolExecutor breadth-first search with synchronized visited set
Thread pool worker queue with active task counter
ConcurrentHashMap key set with ExecutorService level batches
